name: Modern SEO - M1L3 How Google and AI Actually Work
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 1 Foundation and Diagnosis](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-1-foundation-and-diagnosis) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

# Summary
The theory behind the course (4:40). In local SEO you rank the [Google Business Profile](lib:brain-google-business-profile), not the website. Every article, internal link and sponsorship serves that goal: ranking the GBP in the top 3 farther and farther from its address.

# Key concepts
- **Three ranking factors:**
  - **Proximity:** distance between searcher and business. Cannot be changed.
  - **Relevance:** "why we write content." Topical (what services you provide) and geographic (what areas you serve).
  - **Trust:** "a fancy word for quality links"; Google verifying you are a legitimate local business.
- **Overcome the proximity negative.** More relevance and trust expand the radius where the GBP shows top 3.
- **Only the top 3 counts.** "Fourth position is invisible." The core metric is the top 3 percentage of the rank map.
- **Google is math.** A machine learning system maximizing "user happiness through goal completion," measured by engagement.
- **Open book SEO.** Search the keyword; Google shows what it rewards. Do not try to trick it.
- **ChatGPT and Bing (instructor claim).** ChatGPT is the AI tool that matters for local discovery; because of the Microsoft and OpenAI partnership, he says ChatGPT relies on Bing's index, so a business needs a Bing for Business profile too.
- **Same signals work on both:** consistent business info, clear service descriptions, verified citations.

# Checklist
- Tie every content, link or sponsorship task to ranking the GBP.
- Track top 3 percentage as the main success metric.
- Build topical relevance, geographic relevance and trust.
- Search the target keyword and review what ranks before deciding what to build.
- Bing business profile in place; information consistent across platforms; citations verified.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Frame work for [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub), [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) and [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub) around "does this help the GBP rank top 3 farther from the address?" and report top 3 percentage as the headline metric.
- Open book research before content fits Kim's rule to validate keywords (in [Search Atlas](lib:brain-search-atlas) and Keyword Planner) before drafting. See [SEO Blog Writing Standards](lib:brain-seo-blog-writing-standards).
- Recommend Kim check each client's Bing business listing matches the GBP, treating the ChatGPT link as the instructor's claim.

# Caveats and open questions
- The ChatGPT-relies-on-Bing claim needs checking before it is told to a client.
- Audio narrows trust to links; the slide says Google verifies legitimacy. Lesson 4 adds Chamber links and citations as trust signals.
- No source given for the three-factor model.
